_about: Generated by scripts/sync-trinity-facts.mjs from ivanminier/trinity-site data/facts.json. Do not edit by hand; edit the canonical file and re-sync.

peaks_beds.label: Trinity Peaks beds
peaks_beds.meaning: First- and second-year residence-hall beds in new Trinity Peaks wings. Includes resident-assistant beds; excludes staff apartments.

peaks_height.label: Trinity Peaks height
peaks_height.value: No part of Trinity Peaks appears taller than six floors: wings of 5-6 residential floors (up to six full stories) sit on a ground floor set partly below ground, with a hidden seventh level holding the upper floors of duplex rooms.
peaks_height.meaning: The author's design intent. Height in feet is untested; six visible floors may exceed the adopted 55-foot ceiling depending on floor heights and how height is measured, so Peaks may also need a zoning amendment.

rise_beds.label: Trinity Rise baseline beds
rise_beds.meaning: Apartment-style beds for juniors, seniors, and transfer students. The author's height target is now 8-12 stories; the bed count has not been re-tested at that height.

rise_height.label: Trinity Rise height target
rise_height.meaning: Authored massing target. Height in feet is untested; at any plausible floor height it is well above the adopted 55-foot ceiling and the tabled 2022 80-foot recommendation, so it would need a zoning amendment. Phase 0 would test the height and the bed count together.

rise_tall.label: Higher-bed Trinity Rise scenario
rise_tall.meaning: An unapproved alternative scenario only. Not part of the 1,750-2,000 figure.

new_beds.label: New-construction beds (baseline)
new_beds.meaning: Trinity Peaks plus the Trinity Rise baseline. New construction only; it does not count retained buildings such as the Cottages.

replacement_beds.label: Existing beds replaced
replacement_beds.meaning: Beds in the halls the plan demolishes: McAuley (about 160) and Mercy (about 182), both from unverified secondary listings, plus the five Back Five halls at 44-45 beds each (220-225, owner-confirmed). Total about 562-567. Broadly consistent with 2022 reporting of roughly 600 students living on Trinity, which may include temporary triples or the Cottages. UVM's designed-bed counts would confirm it.

net_new_beds.label: Net-new beds (conditional)
net_new_beds.meaning: Arithmetic result using about 565 replaced beds. Changes if UVM's designed-bed counts differ.

peaks_net_new.label: Trinity Peaks net-new first/second-year beds (conditional)
peaks_net_new.meaning: Peaks beds minus about 565 replaced beds, if all replaced beds are first/second-year beds. A large expansion even with no enrollment growth; the demand case must be shown with UVM data.

ra_rooms.label: Resident-assistant rooms
ra_rooms.meaning: Staffing assumption. RAs are students; their beds are counted inside the Peaks bed range, not excluded.

staff_apartments.label: Professional staff apartments
staff_apartments.meaning: Staffing assumption; staff apartments are not counted as student beds.

capital_range.label: Illustrative district capital study range
capital_range.meaning: An illustrative study range with unresolved inclusions (soft costs, off-site utilities, escalation, financing, swing housing, and parking are not confirmed as included). Not an estimate, bid, budget request, or UVM commitment.

capital_components.label: Component allowances
capital_components.value: Peaks + Northside Dining $250M-$325M; Trinity Rise $90M-$140M; Trinity Way, Cottages, and enabling work $35M-$65M
capital_components.meaning: Authored allowances that sum to the study range. The Trinity Rise allowance was carried over from the earlier 400-500-bed concept and has not been rebased to the 300-400-bed baseline.

per_new_bed.label: Capital per new bed (cross-endpoint bounds)
per_new_bed.meaning: $375M / 2,000 and $530M / 1,750. Cross-endpoint bounds, not a paired low and high scenario. Capital per bed is not rent.

per_net_new_bed.label: District investment per net-new bed (cross-endpoint bounds)
per_net_new_bed.meaning: $375M / 1,435 and $530M / 1,185. A different metric from cost per new bed; never substitute one for the other.

rise_per_bed.label: Trinity Rise allowance per baseline bed (cross-endpoint)
rise_per_bed.meaning: $90M / 400 and $140M / 300. The width shows the Rise allowance needs rebasing in Phase 0.

zoning_current.label: Adopted Trinity Campus overlay rules (as reported)
zoning_current.value: Sec. 4.5.2(e): 40% lot coverage (subject to its stated exception); 115-foot Colchester Avenue buffer; new construction up to the greater of 35 feet or existing structures on the same parcel, with an absolute 55-foot ceiling; institutional parking and major-impact review references
zoning_current.meaning: From the City's Article 4 document marked updated Feb. 10, 2026, as reported by the Oct. 29, 2026 audit and consistent with older ordinance text and the City FAQ. Not a legal review; a planner must confirm intervening amendments.

pc_2022.label: 2022 Planning Commission recommendation
pc_2022.value: 45 feet at the front, 80 feet beyond the existing buffer, 65-foot Colchester Avenue setback, 60% lot coverage
pc_2022.meaning: A Planning Commission recommendation for a zoning amendment, not adopted law. The City Council tabled it on Feb. 21, 2023.

mou_2023.label: December 2023 draft MOU
mou_2023.value: A draft UVM-Burlington memorandum discussed up to 1,500 new beds across three UVM parcels together (Trinity Campus, 280 East Avenue, and the Waterman block), at least 1.5 beds per undergraduate enrolled above the fall 2023 level, and a term through October 2028.
mou_2023.meaning: A historical draft that required City Council approval. It did not allocate 1,500 beds to Trinity. Reporting emphasized upperclass apartment housing. Adoption could not be confirmed in public records searched on Oct. 29, 2026.

mou_status.label: MOU adoption status
mou_status.meaning: Council was expected to take it up on Feb. 12, 2024; no final vote or amendment was found. The two City links previously cited return 404 and are no longer cited.

catamount_woods.label: Catamount Woods
catamount_woods.value: In August 2023 UVM announced about 540 upperclass apartment beds near Centennial Woods with AAM 15, owner of the neighboring DoubleTree hotel, on UVM land already leased to AAM 15 for parking. The early estimate was about $100M (about $185,000 per bed). UVM paused and then halted the project in May 2024 over rising construction costs.
catamount_woods.meaning: The $185,000 figure is a failed early estimate, not an achievable local unit rate. UVM ownership of the land does not by itself permit other uses: current lease terms, partner consent, South Burlington review, utilities, transportation, and restoration would all need confirmation.

bench_vt.label: Virginia Tech benchmark
bench_vt.value: $280M for 1,200 beds (about $233,000 per bed), authorized June 2026, including hard and soft costs
bench_vt.meaning: A different program, region, area, financing, and scope.

bench_unc.label: UNC benchmark
bench_unc.value: roughly $108M-$109M announced for about 700 beds (about $154,000-$156,000 per bed), May 2025
bench_unc.meaning: An announced project budget, not an actual cost and not a Burlington estimate.

trinity_halls.label: Current Trinity housing
trinity_halls.value: UVM's Trinity complex includes McAuley, Mercy, the Cottages, and the Back Five halls (Hunt, McCann, Ready, Richardson, Sichel).

upperclass_options.label: Existing upperclass apartment-style options
upperclass_options.value: UVM-operated residence halls offer traditional and suite-style rooms. Apartment-style options for upperclass students come through UVM-affiliated partner communities, including Redstone Lofts (on UVM's Redstone campus under a ground lease) and University Commons, and Spinner Place in Winooski. Catamount East, which UVM previously leased for juniors, seniors, and transfer students, is no longer a UVM option.
upperclass_options.meaning: Eligibility, prices, and availability vary by community and must be confirmed with UVM. Trinity Rise would add apartment-style capacity at Trinity; whether demand justifies it is a Phase 0 question.

catamount_east.label: Catamount East (lost UVM apartment capacity)
catamount_east.value: Catamount East, a UVM-managed apartment-style building for juniors, seniors, and transfer students at 61 North Dorset St. in South Burlington (about 147-164 beds), is no longer a UVM housing option: UVM's lease with Larkin Realty ended after the 2025-26 year and the units are rented to the public.
catamount_east.meaning: UVM's own apartment-style capacity for upperclass students shrank by roughly 150 beds. This strengthens the case for studying Trinity Rise, but it does not by itself prove demand for 300-400 new beds; Phase 0 must measure that. Bed counts differ by source (147 on UVM's outdated page, 164 in the Vermont Cynic). UVM's Catamount East page has not been updated.
